chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated that Sahib ibn Ibad narrated that his father narrated, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them):

He said: Ten [qualities] are those by which anyone who meets God shall enter Paradise: bearing witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); confessing to what came from God; establishing prayer; giving alms-tax; pilgrimage to the House; fasting in the month of Ramadan; accepting the guardianship of the friends of God; being free from the enemies of God; and avoiding every intoxicant.

key_terms.شَهَادَةُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: Testimony that there is no god but God
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting in the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics that guarantee entry into Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive synthesis of Islamic practice, uniquely integrating the five pillars with the distinctively Shia concepts of Wilayah and Bara'ah to form a complete spiritual profile. This enumeration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that true faith requires both outward observance (Zahir) and inward allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring that the believer's deeds are validated by their connection to divine authority. The inclusion of avoiding intoxicants further underscores the holistic nature of this path, linking physical purity with spiritual fidelity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-16 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abu Sa’id al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Ado’we quoted Saheeb ibn Ebad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB), “Anyone who meets God while having ten characteristics shall go to Paradise. They are: bearing witness to the fact that ‘There is no god but God’; bearing witness to the fact that ‘Muhammad is God’s Prophet’; confessing to what the Prophet (MGB) has brought from God; saying his prayers; giving the alms-tax; fasting in the month of Ramazan; going on the pilgrimage to the House of God; accepting the Mastery of the Divine Leaders; condemning God’s enemies; and avoiding all intoxicating drinks.”
